question.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=3(x-2)^{3}$ and the point $P(3,3)$ that lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is invertible in the vicinity of $P,$  calculate ${({f}^{-1})}^{′}(3).$

current_example.problem: Consider the function $f(x) = \dfrac{2-3x}{4+5x}$ and the point $P\left(-1,-5\right)$ that lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is invertible in the vicinity of $P,$ determine the slope of $y=f^{-1}(x)$ at the point $\left(-5,-1\right).$
current_example.worked_solution:
We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(-1, -5).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{2-3x}{4+5x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\frac{22}{(4+5x)^{2}} \\ {f}^{′}(-1) & =-22\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(-1, -5)$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(-5, -1)$ lies on $y=f^{-1}(x).$ 

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(-5) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(-5))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(-1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-22)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{22}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
